newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cortecs says insulin trial pleasing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cortecs says insulin trial pleasing.

text.p: Drug research group Cortecs International Ltd said on Monday that it had achieved encouraging results from its preliminary studies into the development of an oral form of insulin.
The company said six fasting human volunteers were dosed with 200 insulin units through a tube into the small intestine during a placebo-controlled cross-over trial.
It said the results showed plasma insulin levels were higher than those observed after the administration of a placebo.
Insulin is used to treat diabetes mellitus and currently has to be injected into the human system.

"These are very encouraging preliminary results in man after years of challenging effort," president Michael Flynn said in a statement. He said the time of response showed that insulin absorption was taking place via the portal vein.
"We see these results as indicating an opportunity to create an oral insulin product and evidence of the versatility of our oral delivery technology for proteins and peptides," Flynn said.
"However, there are still a number of steps to take before we can say we have a product."

Flynn said subsequent studies would involve the use of tablets so that the final delivery system could be observed. If the results of those studies were satisfactory, Cortecs would perform single dose studies in patients with diabetes.
International Diabetes Institute chief executive Paul Zimmet said the developments could have a significant role in the management of non-insulin dependent diabetes.
"Its role could even be explored in insulin dependent patients as well," Zimmet said in the same statement.
At 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), Cortecs shares were steady at A$6.35 on low turnover. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
